newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy tightens criteria for bond specialists.
newsitem.headline: Italy tightens criteria for bond specialists.

text.p: The Italian Treasury and the Bank of Italy said they were tightening up operating criteria for bond market specialists retroactively to July 1, 1996.

Making the announcement on Reuters page BITG, the authorities said specialists must trade a single bond for a minimum of four hours before it could be included as an operation qualifying for the status of market specialist.
Specialists are required to trade a certain volume of bonds and certain number of individual bonds to retain their status.

The authorities said that when assessing whether bond specialists had met volume requirements in the course of the year they would ignore 15 percent of the most heavily traded sessions or five percent of the least heavily traded sessions.
Market sources said this was in order to make specialists maintain a certain level of volume throughout the year and to prevent artificial trades.
The authorities said from January 1, 1997 these criteria would also apply to primary bond market traders.
